title: The replica that replayed history
blurb: Offsets expired and retries applied twice.
prompt: A target region re-applied three months of changes after a quiet period, and a duplicated apply created orphan rows, because the draft stored offsets with a TTL and dropped the change id on some retry paths. Review it, fix it, and prove offsets are durable and applies are idempotent.
aiNote: The draft keeps per-shard offsets in an expiring cache key, so idleness silently rewinds a shard to zero, and its apply retry path omits the change id, so an apply that succeeded before the timeout is applied a second time.
testIdea: Expire the offset key and assert replication halts or resumes from the confirmed offset, not zero; time out an apply and assert the retry carries the same change id and the target shows one row; sample digests across regions after a divergence test.
followUps: What clock assumptions does last-write-wins make?
When is manual conflict resolution the right policy?
How do you prove two regions converged?
